features.name: glucose_normalized
features.description: Plasma glucose concentration normalized to training set mean and std, providing a standardized continuous score centered at zero for linear margin separation
features.expected_model_benefit: Directly normalized glucose is the strongest single predictor; standardization improves SVM margin geometry

features.name: bmi_normalized
features.description: Body mass index normalized to training set mean and std, capturing obesity severity as a smooth continuous score
features.expected_model_benefit: Standardized BMI improves linear separability for obesity-related metabolic risk

features.name: age_normalized
features.description: Age normalized to training set mean and std, providing a smooth continuous age risk score
features.expected_model_benefit: Standardized age contributes linearly to SVM margin for age-related metabolic risk

features.name: glucose_bmi_composite
features.description: Weighted composite of normalized glucose and BMI scores, combining two strong metabolic risk indicators into a single linear projection
features.expected_model_benefit: Linear combination of top two predictors approximates a useful projection direction for SVM hyperplane

features.name: insulin_log_normalized
features.description: Log-transformed insulin level normalized by training mean of log-insulin, reducing right skew for smoother linear feature
features.expected_model_benefit: Log transformation reduces insulin skewness, improving linear SVM performance on this highly skewed feature

features.name: pedigree_log_normalized
features.description: Log-transformed diabetes pedigree function normalized to reduce skew, capturing genetic risk as a smooth continuous score
features.expected_model_benefit: Normalized pedigree score provides smooth genetic risk signal for linear margin

features.name: glucose_age_interaction
features.description: Product of normalized glucose and normalized age, capturing the interaction between high glucose and older age as a metabolic risk amplifier
features.expected_model_benefit: Interaction term approximates a nonlinear boundary in linear SVM feature space, capturing joint risk elevation

features.name: pregnancies_normalized
features.description: Number of pregnancies normalized to training mean and std, capturing reproductive history as a continuous risk score
features.expected_model_benefit: Standardized pregnancy count contributes to linear margin for parity-related metabolic risk

features.name: skin_thickness_normalized
features.description: Triceps skin fold thickness normalized to training mean and std, capturing adiposity as a continuous score
features.expected_model_benefit: Standardized skin thickness provides smooth adiposity signal complementary to BMI for linear SVM

features.name: blood_pressure_deviation
features.description: Absolute deviation of diastolic blood pressure from training mean, normalized by std, capturing hypertension severity as a non-negative continuous score
features.expected_model_benefit: Blood pressure deviation from normal captures hypertension risk in a smooth, non-negative form useful for linear margins

features.name: metabolic_risk_score
features.description: Weighted composite of normalized glucose, BMI, age, and pedigree scores representing overall metabolic risk as a single continuous projection
features.expected_model_benefit: Multi-factor composite approximates the dominant linear discriminant direction, providing a strong single feature for SVM margin

features.name: insulin_glucose_ratio_score
features.description: Semantic assessment of insulin-to-glucose ratio balance on a continuous scale from 0 to 1, where higher values indicate more physiologically balanced insulin response relative to glucose level. Score accounts for zero insulin values (missing data pattern) and extreme ratios indicating insulin resistance or deficiency.
features.expected_model_benefit: Captures insulin resistance signal as a smooth normalized score, providing a physiologically meaningful feature for linear SVM that raw ratio cannot due to zero-inflation
